title: The four-drummer Six Beasts band at the Holland Inn
summary: He describes a dance band with four drummers on different instruments, including Monk Hazel on mellophone, and playing the Two Bits Club.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: You didn't pay any attention to Monk Hazel or Ash?
I knew it. And growing up, those weren't the guys you listened to.
No, I mean, no, they were not. They were good jazz, good players. I don't say that they were Dixieland or, we had a band once at the Holland Inn. I had four drummers in it.
Four drummers? At the same time?

The Six Beasts Band, it was four drummers. We had Monk Hazel playing mellophone. Ray Benitez was playing bass. Jack Otto was playing piano. Jack Otto was playing drums. And I was playing piano, who was also a drummer. And I was the name of Colomaz, who was a alto, a tenor saxophone player. That was the band. They had four drummers. And all of them playing different instruments. I mean, Monk was playing the mellophone. Not French horn, he played mellophone.
No, it was a dance. It was a dance. Dance, nightclub.
Yeah. You didn't do anything with all the doubling.
I mean, there are bands that used to do that.
No, we used to play at the famous, at the Two Bits Club. You know who owned it? The Hip Ginley was the one that owned it. Hip Ginley owned it. He was, it was at that time, he was in good.
